title: 7-year-old boy feeling unwell
arrival: A 7-year-old boy is brought in by his father after a day of feeling unwell.
keyCriterion: Red — Disability: altered mental status (continuously irritable) with stiff neck
feedbackWhy: He is continuously irritable, which is an altered mental status, and his neck is stiff. Altered mental status with a stiff neck, hypothermia or fever meets a red Disability criterion, so he should be moved to the high acuity area immediately.
reviewNote: CLINICIAN REVIEW REQUIRED: confirm that continuous irritability counts as altered mental status here, and that AVPU A is right for him. The temperature is normal on purpose so the stiff neck is the second finding. Age band 5-12 years (HR 70-140, RR 10-30). Every value is proposed.

design.intendedChallenge: Altered mental status becomes a red criterion when it comes with a stiff neck, hypothermia or fever. A stiff neck is found only by checking.
design.expectedCommonError: triaging as green or yellow because he is awake, has a normal temperature and has no obvious distress.

airway_red.text: No stridor. No chest indrawing. No central cyanosis.

circulation_red.text: Pulse strong. Extremities warm. Capillary refill 2 seconds. No bleeding. Eyes not sunken. Skin pinch returns at once. Drinking normally.

disability_red.text: Continuously irritable and difficult to settle. Resists bending his neck forward. No convulsions.

other_red.text: No trauma, poisoning, threatened limb, snake bite or scrotal pain.

airway_yellow.text: No swelling of the mouth, throat or neck. No wheezing.

circulation_yellow.text: Drinking normally. No vomiting or diarrhoea. Not pale. Mouth moist.

disability_yellow.text: Continuously irritable and difficult to settle. No severe pain reported.

other_yellow.text: No rash. No trauma. No visible wasting. No swelling of both feet. No headache reported. No known surgical diagnosis.
